segments.text:
V. 50.
After he had cried with a loud voice—To ſhew that his Life was ſtill whole in him. He diſmiſſed his ſpirit—So the Original Expreſſion may be literally tranſlated: An Expreſſion admirably ſuited to our LORD's Words, John x. 18. No man taketh my life from me, but I lay it down of myſelf. He died by a voluntary Act of his own, and in a Way peculiar to Himſelf. He alone of all Men that ever were, could have continued alive even in the greateſt Tortures, as long as He pleaſed, or have retired from the Body whenever He had thought ſit. And how does it illuſtrate that Love which He manifeſted in his Death? inaſmuch as He did not uſe his Power to quit his Body, as ſoon as it was faſtened to the Croſs, leaving only an inſenſible Corpſe, to the Cruelty of his Murderers: But continued his Abode in it, with a ſteady Reſolution, as long as it was proper. He then retired from it, with a Majeſty and Dignity, never known or to be known in any other Death: Dying if one may ſo expreſs it, like the Prince of Life.
